Factory catalog (predefined Web Protection Profiles)

The vendor-predefined FortiWeb Web Protection Profiles, stored once per firmware version, build and REST API version, so a deep rediscovery does not re-read them on every sweep; compare them between builds and save one as a template.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsregistry.view operations.template_save
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile → Factory catalog, or Template Library → Factory catalog (URL /web/factory-catalog/)

What is it?#

Every FortiWeb ships the same set of predefined (factory) Web Protection Profiles, such as Inline Standard Protection. The Factory catalog stores each of them once per firmware version, build number and REST API version, the first time a deep rediscovery reads them. Later deep rediscoveries rebuild those profiles from the catalog instead of reading every sub-table from the appliance again. The page lets you browse the stored profiles, compare a profile between two builds and save one as a template.

What does it do?#

  • Keeps one entry per predefined profile (Inline WPP or Offline WPP) per firmware build and API version. A newer build can add fields to the same profile, so each build has its own entries.
  • Fills and reuses entries during the deep pass of a rediscovery:
    • First deep pass on a build — reads the predefined profiles in full and stores the complete tree, every object it names and every read it made.
    • Next deep passes — rebuild a predefined profile from the entry, without its sub-table reads, but only when the appliance's own rows (the profile and every object it names, including the sub-table row counters) match the entry. The rebuilt tree keeps the appliance's own usage counters. Anything that does not match is read in full.
    • Weekly full read — an entry whose last full read is older than 7 days is read in full again by the next deep pass.
  • Marks an entry ambiguous when two appliances on the same build agree on the profile's rows but disagree below them. That profile is then always read in full on that build.
  • Never stores a profile whose full read had a failed request.
  • Shows each profile's full tree, compares the same profile between two builds field by field, and saves an entry as a template.

The firmware is read live from the appliance (its status) at the start of the deep pass, not taken from the appliance record.

From packs (3.0). API and knowledge packs carry a factory section: the predefined profiles the SATOM team captured per build. Imported entries say which pack they were captured from. An entry this node captured from its own appliance is never replaced by a pack, and a pack entry is used only when the appliance's own top-level rows match it — and is re-read in full once older than the weekly window, like any entry. See API library.

Requirements#

  • At least one FortiWeb on which a deep rediscovery has run: open its Rediscovery page and start a sweep with Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) on. See Rediscovery.
  • The appliance must report a firmware build. An appliance whose firmware cannot be determined keeps the full read and adds nothing to the catalog.
  • The catalog must not be switched off on the node (SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG=0, see Advanced).

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the catalog, an entry, and the comparison page registry.view
Save as template from an entry operations.template_save
Fill or refresh the catalog (start a deep rediscovery, tick Re-read predefined WPPs in full) appliances.apply on the Rediscovery page

🔑Permission — Without the permission

Without registry.view the Factory catalog buttons on the Web Protection Profile page and the Template Library are hidden, and opening the URL directly returns 403 Forbidden. Without operations.template_save the entry page does not show the Save as template form. The seeded Viewer, Operator and Administrator profiles all have registry.view; only Operator and Administrator have operations.template_save.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the Web Protection Profile page that carries the Factory catalog button is at FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile (FortiWeb's own menu); the WAF group is gone.

How to use#

Open the catalog#

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM, open FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile and click Factory catalog, or open the Template Library and click Factory catalog.
  2. The Firmware row lists every build the catalog holds, newest first, as 8.0.3 build 93 · API v2.0 with the number of profiles. A yellow number on a build counts variants marked ambiguous.
  3. Click a build. The table lists its profiles:
Column Meaning
Profile The predefined profile's name; click it to open the entry.
Type Inline WPP or Offline WPP.
Objects Objects and sub-table rows in the stored tree.
Status verified, due for a full read (the next deep pass reads it in full), or ambiguous (hover for the reason).
Last full read When and from which appliance it was last read in full.
Rebuilt How many times a deep pass rebuilt the profile from this entry.
Other builds The same profile on other builds; click one to compare.

Read one entry#

The entry page shows Firmware, REST API, Status, Read from (the appliance and time of the first read), Last full read (with the number of full reads), Rebuilt from here, Objects / recorded reads and Content hash. Expand Full tree to see the profile as the deep pass built it; nested objects and sub-table rows are under "_deep".

When the same build holds more than one variant of the profile, Variants on this build links to a comparison between them. Compare with lists the same profile on other builds.

Compare a profile between two builds#

  1. Click a build under Other builds (list) or Compare with (entry page).
  2. The comparison lists every difference as added, removed or changed, with the field path and the value on each build. Paths read field for a profile field, sub-table[row] for a row and named_object[name].field below a referenced object.
  3. Identical profiles show the badge identical and The vendor shipped the same profile on both.

Internal handles and usage counters are not compared. Each kind of difference is cut at 400 rows (Showing the first 400 of each kind.).

Save an entry as a template#

  1. Open the entry.
  2. Under Save as template, keep or change the name and click Save.
  3. The flash reads Saved "<name>" vN for FortiWeb <firmware> (pending approval). and the template opens in the Template Library.

The template is a Web Protection Profile template, stamped with the entry's firmware and API version, provenance factory, and the appliance the entry was read from. Its note starts with From the factory catalog:. It lands pending and goes through the usual approval. See Template library.

❗Important — Approving deploys it

Approving a Web Protection Profile template starts a rollout to every FortiWeb visible to you, after the firmware compatibility check. A template saved from the catalog is no exception.

Refresh the catalog now#

On the appliance's Rediscovery page, switch on Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) and Re-read predefined WPPs in full, then start the sweep. Every predefined profile is read in full and the catalog entries for that build are refreshed. The catalog link next to the switch opens this page.

Example#

🧪Example — What changed in the vendor defaults after an upgrade

  1. fweb-01 runs 7.6.8 and fweb-02 was upgraded to 8.0.3. Both had a deep rediscovery, so the catalog holds both builds.
  2. Open Factory catalog, pick the 8.0.3 build and find Inline Standard Protection.
  3. In Other builds, click the 7.6.8 build. The comparison lists the fields 8.0.3 added to the profile as added and any changed defaults as changed.
  4. To use the 8.0.3 profile as a baseline, open its entry, name it wpp-standard-803 and click Save. An administrator reviews it in the Template Library.

Result#

  • A deep rediscovery reports what the catalog did on its result line, for example Factory catalog (8.0.3 build 93 · API v2.0): 18 predefined WPP(s) from the factory catalog, 2 read in full, plus N new in the catalog, N marked ambiguous or N not stored (a read failed) when they apply.
  • Saving an entry as a template creates a pending template and writes the audit entry factory_catalog.save_template (entry, firmware, build, API version, template name and version).

Troubleshooting#

The page says "Empty."#

Possible causes - No deep rediscovery has run on a FortiWeb since the catalog existed. - The deep rediscoveries ran on appliances whose firmware could not be read.

Solution 1. Open a FortiWeb's Rediscovery page, switch on Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) and start the sweep.

Verification — the result line contains Factory catalog (…) with N new in the catalog, and the build appears on this page.

"The catalog is switched off on this node (SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG=0) …"#

Possible causes — The node's service environment sets SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG=0. Every deep pass then reads every predefined profile in full and nothing is added.

Solution — Remove the variable (or set it to 1) in the service environment and restart the SATOM service.

Verification — the warning is gone and the next deep rediscovery adds entries.

A profile shows "ambiguous"#

Possible causes — Two appliances on the same build serve the same top-level rows for the profile with different sub-tables (the reason reads another appliance on this build serves the same top-level rows with different sub-tables; always read in full), for example because a sub-table row of the predefined profile was edited on one of them.

Solution — Nothing is required: the profile is always read in full on that build, so the deep layer stays correct. Use Variants on this build to see what differs.

"This entry does not hold every read the template needs. Save the profile as a template from an appliance running … instead."#

Possible causes — Building the template needs a read that was not recorded when the entry was captured.

Solution — Open the Web Protection Profile page of an appliance on that firmware and use Save as template there. See Web Protection.

The result line says "N not stored (a read failed)"#

Possible causes — A request failed while a predefined profile was read in full (transport error, authentication, HTTP 5xx). An incomplete tree is never stored.

Solution — Fix the cause and run the deep rediscovery again. The profile is read in full until a complete read has been stored.

The result line says "catalog not updated: …"#

Possible causes — Writing the entries to the database failed. The deep capture itself is unaffected.

Solution — Read the reason, then run the deep rediscovery again.

A predefined profile is read in full on every sweep#

Possible causes - The entry is ambiguous. - The appliance reports no firmware build, so it has no catalog entries. - Re-read predefined WPPs in full is switched on. - The catalog is switched off on the node (SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG=0).

Solution — Check the profile's status here, the warning at the top of this page and the switch on the Rediscovery page.

Advanced#

Advanced Environment variables
Variable Default Effect
SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG on 0 (or false, off, no) switches the catalog off: every predefined profile is read in full and nothing is stored.
SATOM_FACTORY_REVERIFY_DAYS 7 Days (minimum 1) after which an entry is read in full again.
Advanced What the catalog cannot see

The match is made on the appliance's own top-level rows, including the sub-table row counters. Those counters catch rows added or removed, not a sub-table row edited in place on one appliance. Two defences cover that case: every entry is read in full again after SATOM_FACTORY_REVERIFY_DAYS days, and a full read that finds the same top-level rows with a different tree marks the profile ambiguous, after which it is always read in full on that build.

Advanced How a profile is rebuilt

Only a profile the appliance marks as predefined is a candidate; every other profile is walked as before. A rebuilt profile is produced by the same deep capture code from the same answers: top-level lists come from the appliance, and the scoped sub-table reads come from the reads recorded when the entry was captured. Entries are kept in the factory_catalog database table. The catalog is FortiWeb only.
